name: ALL DOMAINS — Social Post (webhook → FB Page + IG → ledger)
source: proposed patch — NOT applied to Make
design: IDEMPOTENCY (P0, was P2): on 2026-09-21 the batch fired 21 executions for 14 tenants and double-posted REAPES and PX on live Pages. The scenario has no dedup, so a re-fire is indistinguishable from a new request. Module 11 derives a dedup key and module 12 checks it BEFORE anything is published.

The key is derived from tenant + message + day, NOT from a caller-supplied request_id alone. That matters: the re-fire that caused the incident sent identical content to the same tenant, so a derived key catches it with zero changes to any caller. A caller-supplied request_id is honoured when present.

Module 7 resolves page_id / ig_account_id / eligibility ONCE as roundtrip variables, so the post modules and the ledger rows read the same resolved values and a ledger row can prove where a post went.
Router 8 replaces the straight line. Route 0 = replay short-circuit, Route 1 = Facebook, Route 2 = Instagram, Route 3 = receipt + respond. Routes run in order, so the response is emitted last.

Route 3 has no filter beyond the dedup gate, so the caller always gets a reply even when a channel is skipped. Moving the response to the end of the main line instead would let a false IG filter swallow the reply entirely.
Both send modules get a resume handler; a channel failure becomes a status instead of aborting before the reply.
The receipt write is GUARDED on a successful publish. An unguarded write would reproduce exactly the 6324097 defect this same branch fixes — marker before proof.
dedupeDatastore: new — do not reuse 152269 (Phillips call outcomes)

steps.label: NEW — derive dedupe_key (caller request_id, else tenant+sha256(message)+day)

routes.label: NEW — replay short-circuit. Nothing is posted twice.

NEW — record the receipt only when Facebook actually published. Writing it unconditionally would repeat the Phillips mistake: a failed publish would lock the key and the retry would be suppressed. Every IG-mapped tenant is also FB-mapped, so "FB posted" is the right condition.
